answer: Persistent Attention Ledger: identities accrue weight only through low-rate, unpredictable check-ins over many epochs; a zephyr of sporadic activity earns nothing. Each identity must answer a signed timing challenge drawn from recent ledger state, and missed windows decay weight toward a nadir that resets accumulated standing. Because challenge cadence is randomized and per-identity, an attacker pays the karst-like cost of continuously staffing and scheduling every fake identity for months, with no bulk shortcut, so marginal cost scales linearly with cluster size.
